correctness.rationale: Construct GP(8,3) by u_i-u_(i+1), u_i-v_i and v_i-v_(i+3), with 16 vertices and 24 edges. Test each subset S for domination and for each outside vertex v the existence of a selected adjacent defender u whose replacement gives ordinary domination. Exhaustive independent bitmask code over all subsets of sizes 0..7 returns none of size below seven and 336 size-seven secure dominating configurations. Exhaustively building secure-to-secure one-vertex jumps yields 1392 edges, one connected component, eccentricities 288 at seven and 48 at eight. Restricting to adjacent slides yields 528 edges, one 288-vertex component and 24 isolated K2 components, with degree and eccentricity histograms stated in the result. A second exact incidence-model verifier explicitly checks an isomorphism and agrees; no randomized inference is used.

evidence: Burger et al. algorithms establish general secure-domination detection, and edge-stability modifies the host graph, not guard positions. Prior zero forcing concerns another property.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The general theory does not imply these sharp GP(8,3) optimum counts or component structure without additional enumeration.
